We saw repeated spikes in inference latency between 02:10–02:18 UTC this morning that directly impacted our checkout flow (70% of requests spiked above our 300ms SLO). Our engineers rolled a hotfix but we'd like to understand the root cause, impact window, and whether Redwood can make us whole for the customer-facing outages.

This is on Brightline's production namespace: brightline-prod. We're sensitive to token costs — the last bill for May jumped because of retries. Can we get a timeline and a proposed remediation/credit?

Best,

Subject: Re: Intermittent inference latency impacting checkout — timeline + estimate

Folks — attaching the incident timeline and a short RCA extract. TL;DR: a control-plane rollout caused a transient routing misconfiguration that increased queueing on the us-west pool for 8 minutes (02:10–02:18 UTC). Peak error rate remained low but tail latency rose due to a batching edge-case in the runtime; KV cache warming amplified the effect for some long-running sessions.

Impact estimate (preliminary):
- Affected window: 2027-05-27T02:10:00Z — 2027-05-27T02:18:00Z
- Affected requests: ~18k requests (brightline-prod namespace)
- Estimated billable tokens impacted: ~240k tokens

Proposed customer-facing make-good (draft):
- Immediate: one-time account credit equivalent to $4,500 (applied to next invoice)
- Operational: 30-day trial extension on Brightline's reserved tier evaluation to help them stabilize ongoing tests
- Tech: priority RCA follow-up and postmortem meeting next week

Attachments: incident_timeline_20270527.pdf (attached)

Notes: I'm marking this as high priority for the reliability team to validate the kernel-selection patch we rolled this morning.

-Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
